messages:
jess: Hi team — escalated from BrightHealth. Their rerank endpoint started returning different scores for identical payloads after model update yesterday. Also seeing intermittent 401s and a billing spike. Full thread from customer attached.

amira: Oof. Do we have customer org id/route? Can you paste example payload + two responses that differ?

jess: org=bright-health, route=/v1/rerank. Example request (sent twice, 10s apart):
```json
{"query":"insurance coverage for knee surgery","candidates":["plan A","plan B","plan C"],"top_k":3}
```
Responses:
- run 1: scores [0.8724, 0.6241, 0.2103]
- run 2: scores [0.7432, 0.6510, 0.2051]
Same payload, same headers, same request_id pattern (client provided id different each time). They say no prompt changes. Both calls were ~50ms apart.

sam: Noted. Any recent model rollouts? I recall a canary of rerank-small-v2.1 yesterday.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: model-redwood/rerank-small-v2.1-promotion @ 2026-02-12T18:40Z (canary->prod) by @leo

leo: That matches. We promoted v2.1 with quantization profile Q4_0.1. Could quantization change ranking ordering? Unlikely but possible at edge cases.

ops: 401s likely separate — seeing a burst of 401s from the LB at ~18:42Z for that org due to short JWT lifetimes when their client clock skewed. That might have caused retries from client generating duplicate requests (billing spike).

billing-bot: Billing alert: org bright-health shows 3x token consumption between 18:40-18:45 UTC. Most duplicates correlate to client retry headers X-Retry-Count:2. We charged per successful token, duplicates applied.

sam: For the score divergence we should rule out nondeterminism: confirm same model id served, same sequence length, temperature=0, and no prefix cache mismatch. Ask customer for request_id from both calls (if they have) and we can grep logs.

jess: Customer provided request_ids: bh-req-5541 and bh-req-5542. Put to grep.

leo: I pulled logs: both requests served by node gpu-12 in us-west-2; model binary = rerank-small-v2.1-q4_0.1. But I see different tokenization token counts: 14 vs 15 tokens, difference at punctuation normalization.

amira: Tokenization diff could explain score jitter. Which tokenizer version did we ship with v2.1? Any changed normalization rules?

sam: v2.1 bumped tokenizer lib from 1.12.0 -> 1.13.0 which includes aggressive whitespace collapse and new punctuation splitting. That can change input ids -> different embeddings -> different rerank scores. So this is likely the cause.

jess: Customer says they send identical UTF-8 bytes. They expect idempotency. They’re upset because ranking changed for identical payloads.

leo: Actionable plan:
1) Pin bright-health to rerank-small-v2.0 (pre-tokenizer change) immediately.
2) Reprocess the two requests through v2.0 and v2.1 locally to confirm.
3) Run tokenization diff tool on the payloads and share report.
4) Billing: refund duplicate charges and advise client about retry/backoff.

sam: I'll run reproducer and dump token ids + logits. If tokenization explains, we need to document tokenizer change in release notes and flag as breaking for rerank customers.

billing-bot: Started refund flow for org bright-health — provisional credit applied for duplicate requests. Will follow up with finance.

ops: For the 401s we recommend advising the customer to increase JWT refresh tolerance and add exponential backoff. We can also add a note in support KB.

amira: Customer-facing message draft: short apology, explanation that a tokenizer update altered tokenization leading to ranking differences, immediate mitigation (we pinned them to previous model), and we’re issuing a refund. I'll send after engineering confirms.

jess: Owners: sam (repro + tokenization report), leo (pin + rollout fix), billing (refund), amira (customer comms). ETA: EOD PST for initial update.

sam: Reproducer results: v2.0 token ids identical across runs, v2.1 token ids different; logits difference shown. Confirmed tokenizer is root cause. I'll attach minimal dump to the ticket.

leo: Pinned bright-health to rerank-small-v2.0 at 2026-02-12T20:05Z. Will schedule a controlled rollback for other sensitive routes and add a release note.

jess: Thanks everyone. I'll close loop with customer now. :white_check_mark:

amira: Great. Follow-up: create a rolling checklist to catch tokenizer changes for rerank models (unit tests on token id invariance for same bytes).

ops: Logged a postmortem ticket: PM-4532 (tokenizer-release-checks) and assigned to eng-ml.

jess: Will update thread if customer responds. Thanks :heart:
